title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a complete discretely valued field (implicitly p-adic) with valuation ring R_K and a uniformizer or nonzero non-unit π. L/K is a Galois extension, possibly infinite, such as a Z_p-extension or the algebraic closure. R_L is the integral closure of R_K in L, G = Gal(L/K), and hats denote π-adic completions: R̂_L = lim R_L/π^n R_L.

Statement: the closed-field invariants \hat L^G equal \hat K exactly when H^1(G, R_L) (continuous cohomology with discrete coefficients) is killed by a fixed power π^c. The page writes this as ⟺; the argument sketched only proves the 'if' direction.

Tools on the page:
(i) R̂_L^G = lim (R_L/π^n R_L)^G, since invariants commute with inverse limits.
(ii) From 0→R_L→L→L/R_L→0 and H^1(G,L)=0 (additive Hilbert 90 / normal basis, passing to the limit over finite subextensions) one gets 0→R_K→K→(L/R_L)^G→H^1(G,R_L)→0. Hence H^1(G,R_L) ≅ (L/R_L)^G/(K/R_K).

Proof sketch of the 'if' direction:
- Take ℓ ∈ \hat L^G and write ℓ = lim x_n with x_n ∈ L and (x_n−ℓ)/π^n ∈ R̂_L.
- For σ ∈ G, (x_n/π^n)^σ − x_n/π^n ∈ R_L. So the class of x_n/π^n lies in (L/R_L)^G.
- If π^c kills H^1, then π^c x_n/π^n ∈ K + R_L, i.e. x_n ∈ K + π^{n−c}R_L.
- Hence ℓ is a limit of elements of K, so ℓ ∈ \hat K.

This is the cohomological packaging of the Ax–Sen–Tate theorem used in Tate's theory of p-divisible groups (C_p^{G_K} = K). For L = K̄, the needed bound on H^1(G_K, O_{K̄}) is exactly Ax's estimate: |σx−x| ≤ 1 for all σ implies x lies within a bounded distance of K. The page follows 'Gribouillis de Tate sur sa théorie'. These are notes of Tate's (1966) theory, consistent with the cote (Tate letter, May 1966).
errors: The converse (⟹) is asserted but not proved on the page. It is plausible via a diagonal construction (unbounded torsion lets one build a non-K̂ invariant series), but it is not shown and needs care, e.g. completeness assumptions.
H^1(G,L)=0 for infinite G requires continuous/discrete cohomology as a direct limit over finite levels. This is implicit.

ideas.what: Criterion \hat L^G = \hat K via bounded π-torsion of H^1(G,R_L), using the sequence 0→R_K→K→(L/R_L)^G→H^1(G,R_L)→0
ideas.modern_name: Ax–Sen–Tate theorem / almost-étale style bounded cohomology of integers
ideas.where_published: Tate, 'p-divisible groups', Proc. Conf. Local Fields, Driebergen 1966 (publ. 1967)

ideas.what: Invariants of a completion as an inverse limit of invariants mod π^n
ideas.modern_name: commutation of invariants with inverse limits

deep.surprise_reason: These are notes reproducing Tate's own argument (the previous page is titled 'Gribouillis de Tate'). The criterion and proof are standard in Tate/Sen/Ax and the later almost-mathematics literature. Nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: The 'Thm' arrow may be one-directional (⟸) rather than ⟺ in the faint image. Only the 'if' direction is argued.
'killed by π^n for some n' should read 'killed by some power π^c' (a bounded exponent).
Line 3 likely reads 'Hyp L/K Galois, ... ring of integers acted on by G = Gal L/K'.
